attack_mechanism: Probing `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]` in this early-round window exposes an internal representation before all 24 rounds have diffused the input. This mechanism uses the chain `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.e[0][2] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]`. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]` is a nonlinear chi result lane; its bits are deterministic functions of the newly accepted `keccak_in` block and the previous state. On the first calculation step after `accept`, the padded rate block has just been XORed into the persistent state and is being evaluated by the two-round Keccak network. The observation leaks lane-level information about the secret input that is not present as a directly accessible architectural signal.

Sampling `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]` at a fixed cycle offset across repeated operations supplies aligned intermediate values for differential or correlation analysis. This mechanism uses the chain `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.e[0][2] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]`. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][2]` is recomputed for later round pairs and therefore yields a time series of input-dependent values from a nonlinear chi result lane. On subsequent `calc` cycles, feedback from the registered permutation output re-enters the same combinational round network. Combining those observations can recover secret-dependent relationships even when a single lane observation is insufficient to reconstruct the input.
